title: Vietnam tour with Louis Cottrell
summary: A five-week USO-style tour from Saigon, two gigs a day by plane and helicopter, in danger and amid the dead.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What about Vietnam? How did you happen to be there?
Well, Vietnam, I went to Vietnam with Louis Contrell. Went on a five week tour in Vietnam and two weeks in Thailand.

With Contrell, it wasn't much fun. Tell them about it. Kinda rough. Did you go to Saigon? Yeah, Saigon was our headquarters. That's where we landed, Saigon, that's where we lived. We stood in Saigon and we shipped out to the gate, you see, from Saigon. We take a plan to some part of Vietnam. Uh, Vietnam, then the, then the helicopter pick us up and bring us behind the hills, the mountains. And we land down where all the soldiers be. And we played two gigs a day. And we played two gigs a day. Taking a plan ride and a helicopter ride, two gigs a day. And some of the things we went so far from Saigon that we have to stay. You know, we stood overnight. Yeah. Yeah. And sometimes they get a warning that things were dangerous and things like that, you know, and they keep us. It was, oh man, it was terrible, man. And we, you see them packing up dead people in a bag, putting them on the sand, helicopter with us, packing them up. All dead people right there. And we sitting here. You know. Have to use that transportation while they could, you understand? They did, put you right along with them, you know what I mean?
That's the way it was, you know. A frog had a few heart attacks about it. It hurted him. Contra pretty frightened himself.
Did they shoot at you much?

Oh man, you could hear bullocks whistling around us. But I tell you what. They fooled me, you understand? Because I didn't know it was going to be like that. I thought we was going and playing, you know, a USO show. Something like that. You know. That's what I really thought it was going to be. But it was different. It really was different. Everywhere we land, the boss told us we were in danger. Everywhere we land, they fight right there. They used to tell us, the boss tell us, man, what you people doing out here, you know? They'd be glad you came, but if I was you, I would never care what we had. They'd tell us many times.
Did they have any white soldiers there? White soldiers?
Sure, white soldiers. Many, many, many, many white soldiers. White in color. Sure.
Everywhere they had soldiers in Vietnam, we went. We had five weeks of it, doing two jobs a day. Mm-hmm. And every job was different, so you know we went many places.
